newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania hopes to sign IMF accord by end-1997.
newsitem.headline: Albania hopes to sign IMF accord by end-1997.

text.p: Albania hopes to sign either a one-year standby agreement or a three-year agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) by the end of 1997, Finance Minister Arben Malaj told parliament on Tuesday.
Malaj, a Socialist, told parliament an IMF team would visit Albania in early August and said he had already received positive signals from the fund.
"In line with our political will to implement their demands, we could achieve an agreement with the IMF in December. It could be a one-year stand-by accord or a three-year agreement," he said.
He urged the new Socialist-dominated parliament to approve all the necessary fiscal elements for a much-needed deal, saying: "Everything will be conditional on the steps we take."
Parliament will also examine a law on the administration of the remaining high-interest investment schemes.

The collapse of so-called pyramid schemes earlier this year sparked months of violence in Europe's poorest state and led to the ousting of the right-leaning Democratic Party government and the resignation of president Sali Berisha.
Malaj said the government would consider ways of limiting informal loans. "We would allow non-formal credit to be only 10 percent higher than commercial banking rates."

He said the government would continue to service a foreign debt of $688 million which derived from 73 foreign soft credits and accounted for 24.8 percent of GDP. The government's internal debt amounted to 113 billion leks, he added.

The budget deficit was planned to reach 44 billion leks, or 11.6 percent of GDP, this year and inflation was expected to rise to 45-50 percent. "We plan to lower the deficit by increasing revenue," Malaj said.
